Kiểm định thống kê so sánh giữa các nhóm

Author

Duc Nguyen | tuhocr.com

Published

October 30, 2026

Tài liệu biên soạn trong chuyên đề R Statistics

1 Import dataset

Sử dụng dataset students.csv, chọn những bạn đã tốt nghiệp (graduated == 1).

students <- read.csv("students.csv")

df <- students[ , -c(1,3,8,10,12)]

df <- df |> subset(graduated == 1)

row.names(df) <- NULL
# head(df)

1.1 Chia group theo độ tuổi

library(dplyr)

df |> dplyr:::mutate(age_group = case_when(
  
  age >= 30 ~ ">= 30",
  
  age < 30 ~ "< 30",
  
  .default = NA
  
  )) -> df

df$age_group <- factor(df$age_group)

1.2 Subset 50 bạn trong nhóm tuổi

id_upper_30 <- which(df$age_group == ">= 30")

set.seed(1)
sample(x = id_upper_30,
       size = 50,
       replace = F) -> id_upper_30_ok

id_upper_30_ok
 [1] 1486  792   10  700  888  295 1264 1009  470 1193 1573  113  724 1548 1661  904  687  712  866  781  962  434  565 1388 1250 1522 1238  500   91  816 1628
[32]  550 1237 1705 1430 1077  529  658 1637   46  382  492  935 1401 1691  969 1298 1625  180  373
id_under_30 <- which(df$age_group == "< 30")

set.seed(1)
sample(x = id_under_30,
       size = 50,
       replace = F) -> id_under_30_ok

id_under_30_ok
 [1] 1068  714  137  979 1609  493  313  283 1270 1395  628 1362 1593  344 1697   38 1182  766  923  508  919  401 1708 1026  842  895  980  340 1740  583 1514
[32]  119 1496  558 1606  585  934  358  612 1200   41  564  394  260 1281  397   40  455  851 1481
df_sample <- df[ c(id_upper_30_ok, id_under_30_ok) , ]
row.names(df_sample) <- NULL
# aggregate(salary ~ age_group,
#           data = df_sample,
#           FUN = mean)
# điều chỉnh dữ liệu cho nhóm upper luôn cao hơn under
set.seed(1)
df_sample$salary[which(df_sample$age_group == ">= 30")] <- df_sample$salary[which(df_sample$age_group == ">= 30")] + 1500
df_sample <- df_sample[ , -11]

df_sample$ID <- c(1:length(id_upper_30_ok),
                  1:length(id_under_30_ok))

dim(df_sample)
[1] 100  13

2 Independent two-sample | So sánh giữa hai nhóm độc lập

2.1 Parametric independent two-sample t-test

2.1.1 Check normality | Kiểm tra giả thuyết phân bố chuẩn

H0: normality (p-value >= 0.05)

H1: NOT normality (p-value < 0.05)

upper_30 <- df_sample$salary[which(df_sample$age_group == ">= 30")]

under_30 <- df_sample$salary[which(df_sample$age_group == "< 30")]
library(car)

car:::qqPlot(upper_30)
[1] 38 23
car:::qqPlot(under_30)
[1] 33 35
shapiro.test(upper_30)

    Shapiro-Wilk normality test

data:  upper_30
W = 0.96657, p-value = 0.1673
ks.test(x = jitter(upper_30),
        y = "pnorm",
        mean = mean(upper_30),
        sd = sd(upper_30))

    Exact one-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test

data:  jitter(upper_30)
D = 0.1036, p-value = 0.6192
alternative hypothesis: two-sided
library(nortest)
nortest:::lillie.test(upper_30)

    Lilliefors (Kolmogorov-Smirnov) normality test

data:  upper_30
D = 0.10354, p-value = 0.1987
nortest:::ad.test(upper_30)

    Anderson-Darling normality test

data:  upper_30
A = 0.80719, p-value = 0.03421
shapiro.test(under_30)

    Shapiro-Wilk normality test

data:  under_30
W = 0.97963, p-value = 0.5366
ks.test(x = jitter(under_30),
        y = "pnorm",
        mean = mean(under_30),
        sd = sd(under_30))

    Exact one-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test

data:  jitter(under_30)
D = 0.073134, p-value = 0.934
alternative hypothesis: two-sided
library(nortest)
nortest:::lillie.test(under_30)

    Lilliefors (Kolmogorov-Smirnov) normality test

data:  under_30
D = 0.073247, p-value = 0.7217
nortest:::ad.test(under_30)

    Anderson-Darling normality test

data:  under_30
A = 0.37747, p-value = 0.3961

2.1.2 Check variance homogeneity | Kiểm tra giả thuyết phương sai đồng nhất

H0: phương sai giữa các nhóm bằng nhau

H1: có ít nhất một nhóm có phương sai khác biệt

# kiểm định giữa 2 nhóm
# phổ biến nhất, không yêu cầu 2 vector bằng nhau
stats:::var.test(upper_30,
                 under_30)

    F test to compare two variances

data:  upper_30 and under_30
F = 1.0588, num df = 49, denom df = 49, p-value = 0.8424
alternative hypothesis: true ratio of variances is not equal to 1
95 percent confidence interval:
 0.6008322 1.8657694
sample estimates:
ratio of variances 
           1.05878 
stats:::var.test(salary ~ age_group,
                 data = df_sample)

    F test to compare two variances

data:  salary by age_group
F = 0.94448, num df = 49, denom df = 49, p-value = 0.8424
alternative hypothesis: true ratio of variances is not equal to 1
95 percent confidence interval:
 0.5359719 1.6643581
sample estimates:
ratio of variances 
         0.9444835 
# kiểm định giữa 2 hay nhiều nhóm
# mạnh khi dữ liệu có phân phối chuẩn
# nhạy với vi phạm giả định chuẩn
stats:::bartlett.test(df_sample$salary, # vector numeric
                      df_sample$age_group) # vector categorical

    Bartlett test of homogeneity of variances

data:  df_sample$salary and df_sample$age_group
Bartlett's K-squared = 0.039555, df = 1, p-value = 0.8424
# kiểm định giữa 2 hay nhiều nhóm
# phù hợp khi dữ liệu chuẩn và không chuẩn
library(car)
# dữ liệu phân bố chuẩn
car::leveneTest(df_sample$salary,
                df_sample$age_group,
                center = "mean")
Levene's Test for Homogeneity of Variance (center = "mean")
      Df F value Pr(>F)
group  1  0.7997 0.3734
      98               
# dữ liệu lệch chuẩn Brown–Forsythe test (biến thể của Levene's test)
car::leveneTest(df_sample$salary,
                df_sample$age_group,
                center = "median")
Levene's Test for Homogeneity of Variance (center = "median")
      Df F value Pr(>F)
group  1  0.5789 0.4486
      98               
# kiểm định giữa 2 hay nhiều nhóm
# khi dữ liệu không có phân bố chuẩn
# Performs a Fligner-Killeen (median) test of the null that the variances in each of the groups (samples) are the same.
stats::fligner.test(df_sample$salary,
                   df_sample$major)

    Fligner-Killeen test of homogeneity of variances

data:  df_sample$salary and df_sample$major
Fligner-Killeen:med chi-squared = 16.767, df = 5, p-value = 0.004964

2.1.3 Vẽ đồ thị boxplot

boxplot(upper_30, under_30,
        las = 1,
        names = c("upper_30", "under_30"),
        main = "Salary | upper_30 vs under_30")

2.1.4 Kiểm định two-sample t-test

2.1.4.1 Dữ liệu phân bố chuẩn và phương sai đồng nhất

NORMALITY | VARIANCE HOMOGENEITY (EQUAL VARIANCE)

# TWO-TAILS
# H0: trung binh upper_30 = trung binh under_30
# H1: trung binh upper_30 ≠ trung binh under_30

t.test(upper_30,
       under_30,
       var.equal = TRUE,
       paired = FALSE,
       alternative = "two.sided") 

    Two Sample t-test

data:  upper_30 and under_30
t = 2.2423, df = 98, p-value = 0.0272
alternative hypothesis: true difference in means is not equal to 0
95 percent confidence interval:
  538.9874 8836.1662
sample estimates:
mean of x mean of y 
 45855.14  41167.57 
# LEFT-TAIL
# H0: trung binh upper_30 ≥ trung binh under_30
# H1: trung binh upper_30 < trung binh under_30

t.test(upper_30,
       under_30,
       var.equal = TRUE,
       paired = FALSE,
       alternative = "less")

    Two Sample t-test

data:  upper_30 and under_30
t = 2.2423, df = 98, p-value = 0.9864
alternative hypothesis: true difference in means is less than 0
95 percent confidence interval:
     -Inf 8159.009
sample estimates:
mean of x mean of y 
 45855.14  41167.57 
# RIGHT-TAIL
# H0: trung binh upper_30 ≤ trung binh under_30
# H1: trung binh upper_30 > trung binh under_30

t.test(upper_30,
       under_30,
       var.equal = TRUE,
       paired = FALSE,
       alternative = "greater")

    Two Sample t-test

data:  upper_30 and under_30
t = 2.2423, df = 98, p-value = 0.0136
alternative hypothesis: true difference in means is greater than 0
95 percent confidence interval:
 1216.144      Inf
sample estimates:
mean of x mean of y 
 45855.14  41167.57

2.1.4.2 Dữ liệu phân bố chuẩn và phương sai không đồng nhất

NORMALITY and VARIANCE HETEROSKEDASTICITY (UNEQUAL VARIANCE)

Sử dụng t-test cải tiến | Welch Two Sample t-test

t.test(upper_30,
       under_30,
       var.equal = FALSE,
       paired = FALSE,
       alternative = "two.sided")

    Welch Two Sample t-test

data:  upper_30 and under_30
t = 2.2423, df = 97.92, p-value = 0.0272
alternative hypothesis: true difference in means is not equal to 0
95 percent confidence interval:
  538.9451 8836.2085
sample estimates:
mean of x mean of y 
 45855.14  41167.57

2.1.4.3 Effect size

Compute the effect size for t-test. T-test conventional effect sizes, proposed by Cohen, are: 0.2 (small effect), 0.5 (moderate effect) and 0.8 (large effect).

library(rstatix)
rstatix:::cohens_d(salary ~ age_group,
                      data = df_sample,
                   var.equal = FALSE,
                   paired = FALSE)
# A tibble: 1 × 7
  .y.    group1 group2 effsize    n1    n2 magnitude
* <chr>  <chr>  <chr>    <dbl> <int> <int> <ord>    
1 salary < 30   >= 30   -0.448    50    50 small    
library(effectsize)

effectsize:::cohens_d(
  upper_30,
  under_30,
  paired = F
)
Cohen's d |       95% CI
------------------------
0.45      | [0.05, 0.84]

- Estimated using pooled SD.

2.2 Nonparametric

2.2.1 Independent two-sample Mann–Whitney U test

Mann–Whitney U test (aka Wilcoxon Rank Sum test) compares two independent groups. Dành cho dữ liệu không đạt phân phối chuẩn (gần chuẩn).

Nonparametric không yêu cầu giả định NORMALITY và VARIANCE HOMOGENEITY.

wilcox.test(upper_30,
       under_30,
       paired = FALSE,
       alternative = "two.sided")

    Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction

data:  upper_30 and under_30
W = 1563, p-value = 0.03122
alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0
library(rstatix)
# nếu chỉ có so sánh giữa 2 nhóm thì không cần adjust p-value
rstatix:::wilcox_test(salary ~ age_group,
                      data = df_sample,
                      paired = FALSE,
                      p.adjust.method = "none",
                      alternative = "two.sided") 
# A tibble: 1 × 7
  .y.    group1 group2    n1    n2 statistic      p
* <chr>  <chr>  <chr>  <int> <int>     <dbl>  <dbl>
1 salary < 30   >= 30     50    50       937 0.0312

2.2.2 Effect size

The r value varies from 0 to close to 1. The interpretation values for r commonly in published litterature and on the internet are: 0.10 - < 0.3 (small effect), 0.30 - < 0.5 (moderate effect) and >= 0.5 (large effect).

rstatix:::wilcox_effsize(salary ~ age_group,
                      data = df_sample,
                      paired = FALSE)
# A tibble: 1 × 7
  .y.    group1 group2 effsize    n1    n2 magnitude
* <chr>  <chr>  <chr>    <dbl> <int> <int> <ord>    
1 salary < 30   >= 30    0.216    50    50 small

2.2.3 Independent two-sample Mood’s Median Test

Performs a Mood’s median test to compare medians of independent samples

# https://rcompanion.org/handbook/F_09.html
library(RVAideMemoire)
RVAideMemoire:::mood.medtest(salary ~ age_group,
                      data = df_sample,            
                      exact = FALSE)

    Mood's median test

data:  salary by age_group
X-squared = 1.96, df = 1, p-value = 0.1615

Testing the equality of the distributions of a numeric response variable in two or more independent groups against shift alternatives.

library(coin)

coin:::median_test(salary ~ age_group,
                      data = df_sample)

    Asymptotic Two-Sample Brown-Mood Median Test

data:  salary by age_group (< 30, >= 30)
Z = -1.592, p-value = 0.1114
alternative hypothesis: true mu is not equal to 0

2.3 Áp dụng package

library(ggstatsplot)
library(tidyverse)

set.seed(20)

ggstatsplot:::ggbetweenstats(data = df_sample,
                     x = age_group,
                     y = salary,
                     type = "parametric",
                     var.equal = TRUE,
                     plot.type = "box",
                     pairwise.comparisons = T,
                     pairwise.display = "all",
                     p.adjust.method = "none",
                     centrality.plotting = T,
                     centrality.path = T,
                     digits = 4L,
                       centrality.point.args = list(size = 4, color = "darkred"),
                     centrality.label.args = list(size = 4,
                                                  nudge_x = 0.4,
                                                  segment.linetype = 4),
                     ggtheme = theme_classic(base_size = 12),
                     bf.message = T,
                     results.subtitle = T,
                     caption = "",
                     ggsignif.args = list(size = 0.5,
                                          vjust = 0,
                                          step_increase = 0.1,
                                          textsize = 5),
                     point.args = list(position = ggplot2::position_jitterdodge(dodge.width = 0.6),
                                       alpha = 0.5,
                                       size = 6,
                                       stroke = 0,
                                       na.rm = TRUE)
                     ) 
library(dabestr)

two_groups_unpaired <- dabestr:::load(df_sample,
  x = age_group, y = salary, 
  paired = NULL,
  idx = c("< 30", ">= 30")
)

two_groups_unpaired.mean_diff <-  dabestr::cohens_d(two_groups_unpaired)


print(two_groups_unpaired.mean_diff)
DABESTR v2025.3.15
==================

Good evening!
The current time is 19:59 PM on Friday October 30, 2026.

The character(0) Cohen's d between >= 30 and < 30 is 0.448 [95%CI 0.054, 0.851].
The p-value of the two-sided permutation t-test is 0.0272, calculated for legacy purposes only.

5000 bootstrap samples were taken; the confidence interval is bias-corrected and accelerated.
Any p-value reported is the probability of observing the effect size (or greater),
assuming the null hypothesis of zero difference is true.
For each p-value, 5000 reshuffles of the control and test labels were performed.
dabest_plot(two_groups_unpaired.mean_diff)

library(ggplot2)
library(ggsignif)

options(scipen = 999)

dp <- df[ , c("gender",
              "major",
              "salary")]
dim(dp)
[1] 1753    3
dp <- na.omit(dp)
dim(dp)
[1] 1753    3
p1 <- ggplot(data = dp,
       mapping = aes(x = gender,
                     y = salary,
                     fill = gender)) +

  # geom_boxplot() +

   geom_violin(alpha = 0.1,
              show.legend = F) +

  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.1, height = 0),
             mapping = aes(color = gender),
             alpha = 0.5) +

    stat_summary(fun.data = mean_cl_boot,
               geom ='crossbar',
               width = 0.6,
               alpha = 0.5,
               aes(fill = gender)) +

   ggsignif:::geom_signif(comparisons =  list(c("Male", "Female")),
                         map_signif_level = function(p_ok) {
                           options(scipen = 1)
                           options(digits = 2)
                          capture.output(cat(p_ok)) -> p_ok_final
                         paste0("p", " = ", p_ok_final)

                         },
                         textsize = 4,
                         vjust = -0.5,
                         step_increase = 0.6,
                         test = "t.test",
                         test.args = list(paired = F)
                         ) +

  facet_grid(~ major) +

  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(10000,100000),
                     breaks = seq(from = 10000,
                                  to = 100000,
                                  by = 10000)) +

  theme_bw(base_size = 13) +

  labs(x = "")

# ANOVA type I | variance equal
fit1 <- aov(weight ~ group,
           data = PlantGrowth)

summary(fit1)

---

                            data = PlantGrowth,
                            var.equal = T)

fit2

data:  weight and group
F = 5, num df = 2, denom df = 27, p-value = 0.02

6.1 Check assumption

6.1.1 Normality

library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)
df$major <- factor(df$major)
ggpubr:::ggqqplot(data = df, 
                  x = "salary", 
                  facet.by = "major")
major_ok <- unique(df$major)

for(i in 1:length(major_ok)){
check_normality <- df |> subset(major == major_ok[i])

print(major_ok[i])
kq <- nortest:::ad.test(check_normality$salary)
print(kq)
}

### Lưu ý nếu dữ liệu không đều nhau thì nên thực hiện thủ công trích từng vector kiểm riêng normality
df_wide <- df[ , c("major", "salary")] %>%
  group_by(major) %>%
  mutate(id = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup() %>% as.data.frame() %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = major,
    values_from = salary
  )

df_wide <- df_wide[, -1]
library(MVN)
### Vì dữ liệu df_wide bị NA nên khi thực hiện, package sẽ tự động remove NA, làm sai kết quả.
df_wide <- na.omit(df_wide)
MVN:::mvn(df_wide)

6.4 Post-hoc analysis | Multiple comparisons

6.4.1 Bonferroni

• “bonferroni” Kiểm soát family-wise error rate (FWER), khá bảo thủ • “holm” Kiểm soát FWER, thường ít bảo thủ hơn Bonferroni • “bh” Kiểm soát false discovery rate (FDR)

library(FSA)
